title_en: Deed Tax Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1. Entities and individuals that acquire the ownership of land and buildings within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be the taxpayers of deed tax and shall pay deed tax in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 3. The deed tax rate shall be 3% to 5%.
The specific applicable deed tax rate shall be proposed by the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government within the range specified in the preceding paragraph, shall be determined by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the same level, and shall be filed with the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for record.
Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, in accordance with the procedures set forth in the preceding paragraph, determine differential rates for the transfer of ownership of different types of housing to different entities and in different regions.
Article 5. The amount of deed tax payable shall be calculated by multiplying the tax basis by the specific applicable tax rate.

Article 7. Provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may decide to exempt or reduce deed tax for the following circumstances:
(1) Re-acquisition of ownership of land and buildings due to the requisition or expropriation of land or buildings by the people's government at or above the county level;
(2) Re-acquisition of ownership of housing due to the loss of housing caused by force majeure.
The specific measures for the exemption or reduction of deed tax as provided in the preceding paragraph shall be proposed by the people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, shall be determined by the Standing Committee of the People's Congress at the same level, and shall be filed with the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for record.

Article 8. Where a taxpayer changes the use of the relevant land or buildings or otherwise no longer falls within the circumstances for exemption or reduction of deed tax specified in Article 6 of this Law, the taxpayer shall pay the tax that has been exempted or reduced.

Article 9. The time when the obligation to pay deed tax arises shall be the day on which the taxpayer signs a contract for the transfer of ownership of land and buildings, or the day on which the taxpayer obtains any other document having the nature of a contract for the transfer of ownership of land and buildings.
Article 10. The taxpayer shall declare and pay deed tax before completing the formalities for registration of ownership of land and buildings according to law.

Article 11. After the taxpayer has gone through the tax payment formalities, the tax authority shall issue a deed tax payment certificate. When the taxpayer goes through the formalities for registration of ownership of land and buildings, the immovable property registration authority shall examine the deed tax payment certificate, tax reduction or exemption certificate, or relevant information. Where the deed tax has not been paid in accordance with the provisions, the immovable property registration authority shall not handle the registration of ownership of land and buildings.

Article 12. Where, before the registration of ownership of land and buildings is completed according to law, the contract for the transfer of ownership or the document having the nature of a contract for the transfer of ownership does not take effect, is null and void, is revoked, or is terminated, the taxpayer may apply to the tax authority for a refund of the tax paid, and the tax authority shall handle the refund in accordance with the law.

Article 13. The tax authority shall establish a mechanism for sharing deed tax-related information and for work coordination with relevant departments. The departments of natural resources, housing and urban-rural development, civil affairs, public security, and other relevant departments shall timely provide the tax authority with information related to the transfer of ownership of land and buildings, and shall assist the tax authority in strengthening the administration of deed tax collection.
The tax authority and its staff shall keep confidential the personal information of taxpayers that they have learned in the course of tax collection and administration according to law, and shall not disclose or illegally provide such information to others.

Article 14. Deed tax shall be collected and administered by the tax authority in the place where the land and buildings are located, in accordance with the provisions of this Law and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection.

Article 15. Where a taxpayer, the tax authority, or any of its staff violates the provisions of this Law, legal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection and relevant laws and regulations.

Article 16. This Law shall come into force as of September 1, 2021. The Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Deed Tax promulgated by the State Council on July 7, 1997 shall be simultaneously abolished.
